review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read kernelMeasure and its lemmas in Approximation.lean, including the other places that unfold it with simp. I did not run Lean. The only simp-interface issue I found is that kernelMeasure has no applied-form lemma, so callers unfold the definition inside simp sets. The other simp/simpa calls in the file are local, ad hoc and terminating. I found no loop or competing-rule risk and judged them too minor to report.

findings.problem: kernelMeasure is a plain def with no canonical applied-form lemma, so the proof unfolds it inside a simp set. It adds withDensity_apply by hand and also supplies the measurability fact. The same recipe appears in Approximation.lean in kernelMeasure_univ (`simp [kernelMeasure, MeasureTheory.withDensity_apply, MeasurableSet.univ]`) and kernelMeasure_le_smul_volume (`simp only [kernelMeasure, MeasureTheory.withDensity_apply, hs]`). Each caller therefore exposes the withDensity implementation. If the definition changes, every call site breaks.
findings.proposed_change: In Approximation.lean, next to the definition, add `lemma kernelMeasure_apply (ψ : E → ℝ) {s : Set E} (hs : MeasurableSet s) : kernelMeasure ψ s = ∫⁻ x in s, ENNReal.ofReal (ψ x) ∂volume := withDensity_apply _ hs`. Mark it `@[simp]` only if the measurability side condition is discharged reliably; otherwise use it via `simp [kernelMeasure_apply, hmeas]` or `rw`. Here the proof would then use `kernelMeasure_apply ψ hmeas` followed by `setLIntegral_eq_zero`. The other two lemmas could use it too, with no unfolding of kernelMeasure.
findings.benefit: One lemma replaces the repeated unfolding and withDensity_apply recipe. The measure's implementation stays hidden from downstream proofs. Simp calls involving kernelMeasure become shorter and less fragile.

evidence.excerpt: (volume : Measure E).withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (ψ x)
